header.name: Neuroscience of Decision Making
header.description: The course will introduce how perception,  goals, preferences, motivation of living systems guide their selection of actions and thoughts from several possible options. The course will try to build a mechanistic understanding of the processes in the brain that support decision making and how they are flexibly updated in a dynamically changing environment. Classes will discuss relevant scientific & historical background, salient theoretical models and experimental evidence in various aspects of decision-making. An additional component will involve computational analysis of experimental datasets in this field to make inferences about brain and behaviour. The primary effort would be to make neural mechanisms accessible to the learners, expose them to possible applications and encourage them to find their own avenues of interest for translating the core principles of decision neuroscience.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Describe the basic neural structures involved in decision making and their functions.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Explain the different methods of investigating neural decision making and the rationale behind choosing the methods

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Explain the neural basis of the salient models and concepts of decision making with the help of data from brain and behaviour.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Deconstruct data and draw conclusions from experiment(s) in decision neuroscience.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Utilize the afrometioned concepts to generate and articulate one experimentally testable idea in decision neuroscience.
